fields.title: 1. The Event — Press Reports vs. Original Text vs. Filings
fields.md:
| Date (US) | Fact | Source grade · source |
|---|---|---|
| **2026-09-30** | Defense Secretary Hegseth announces Project Meridian in the Quantico 'State of the Force' speech + the same day a **one-page (4-paragraph) memo** "Commissioning of Project Meridian: The Future of Warfare" — directs Under Secretary for Research and Engineering and CTO **Emil Michael** to commission research 'through partner institutions.' Identify the future battlefield, required weapons and technologies; AI, autonomy, directed energy, robotics, biotechnology; from underground to cislunar space. **Reporting deadline: 120 days after announcement = 2027-01-28**, a declassified public report + a classified annex. **The memo does not name Musk, Luckey or Gingrich** — the designation of the three as co-directors appears in the speech and the Defense Department press release | ③ (government) memo PDF [media.defense.gov](https://media.defense.gov/2026/Sep/30/2004009287/-1/-1/1/COMMISSIONING-OF-PROJECT-MERIDIAN.PDF) · Defense Department press release [war.gov 4615424](https://www.war.gov/News/Releases/Release/Article/4615424/secretary-hegseth-announces-six-major-initiatives-at-quantico-speech/) — **both returned 403 to this round's tools**; contents confirmed via ⑥ [MIXED 10/02 (full summary of the memo)](https://mixed-news.com/en/project-meridian-memo-emil-michael-palmer-luckey-musk/) · [The Next Web 09/30](https://thenextweb.com/news/pentagon-project-meridian-musk-luckey-gingrich) |
| 2026-10-02 | Politico: the Defense Department held **2** meetings (attended by Senator Cotton and the Secretary's brother Phil Hegseth), 9 current and former officials warn of "conflicts of interest," SpaceX holds "2 multibillion-dollar contracts for a classified satellite constellation." Senators Kelly and Shaheen oppose | ⑥ [Politico (Yahoo reprint) 10/02](https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/musk-led-war-commission-triggers-184841551.html) |
| 2026-10-06 | NPR: **SpaceX 2026 US defense contracts exceed $8 billion** (tallied from government contract notices), operates Starshield, **the Defense Department uses Grok**. Defense Department spokesperson: "MITRE is responsible for analysis and recommendations, and conflict-of-interest and information-protection safeguards apply," time horizon 10–20 years. **Whether Musk and Luckey are SGEs or contractors has not been disclosed** — if SGEs, federal criminal law (bar on participating in decisions affecting one's own property interests) applies. Same day, Anduril Navy contract announced (up to $2.9 billion, submarine components — citing CNBC) | ⑤·⑥ [NPR 10/06 (WFAE reprint)](https://www.wfae.org/united-states-world/2026-10-06/elon-musk-and-palmer-luckeys-new-pentagon-roles-raise-ethics-worries) · [NPR Illinois reprint](https://www.nprillinois.org/2026-10-06/elon-musk-and-palmer-luckeys-new-pentagon-roles-raise-ethics-worries) · ⑥ [OCBJ 10/06](https://www.ocbj.com/newsletter-feed/anduril-gets-u-s-navy-contract-for-up-to-2-9b/) |
| 2026-10-29 | POGO letter to the Defense Department — demands that budget expert William Hartung be seated as a member to provide balance, requests a reply by 10/30 (no reply) | ⑥ [Military.com 11/03](https://www.military.com/hegseths-future-of-warfare-panel-is-stacked-with-contractors-who-stand-to-profit-lawsuit-says) |
| **2026-11-02 (Mon)** | **Lawsuit filed** — plaintiffs CREW, Public Citizen and POGO; defendants the Defense Department, Hegseth and Emil Michael; **US District Court for the District of Columbia**. Complaint is 37 pages (court PDF metadata creation 11/2 14:32 ET). Allegations: ① failure to meet FACA procedural and substantive requirements (no charter, closed meetings, unreleased records, unbalanced composition) ② by the MITRE roster, 3 co-directors + 17 participants, **19 of 21 are private citizens** (the government side is only Michael and Air Force Chief Scientist Victoria Coleman) ③ Musk and Luckey are "leaders of and stakeholders in major defense contractors," and other members include Oracle (Catz), a Palantir co-founder (Lonsdale), Axon (Smith), Saronic, Hadrian, Agility Robotics, Stoke Space, etc. ④ no review of whether an existing chartered committee (the Science and Technology Innovation board) could do the work ⑤ the 9/30 (SCIF) and 10/1 (attended by Senators Cotton and Sheehy) meetings were closed ⑥ records requests unanswered. **Relief sought**: voiding the 9/30 memo · barring activity until FACA compliance · preserving and releasing records · barring acceptance or implementation of recommendations in the meantime. The complaint does not allege that "a particular member steered contracts." **Filing alone does not halt the activity** | ⑥ (plaintiff side) [CREW](https://www.citizensforethics.org/legal-action/lawsuits/new-lawsuit-challenges-hegseths-illegal-future-of-warfare-committee/) · [POGO](https://www.pogo.org/press-center/release/statement-on-project-meridian-lawsuit) (403 this round) · complaint PDF [posted by Public Citizen](https://www.citizen.org/wp-content/uploads/CREW-v-DoD-Complaint.pdf) · [posted by CREW (redacted)](https://www.citizensforethics.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/CREW-v-Hegseth-Complaint_Redacted.pdf) — **full text not read with this round's tools (cannot render)**; complaint contents cited from ⑥ [Military.com 11/03](https://www.military.com/hegseths-future-of-warfare-panel-is-stacked-with-contractors-who-stand-to-profit-lawsuit-says) · [Common Dreams 11/03](https://www.commondreams.org/news/project-meridian-lawsuit) · [Truthout 11/03](https://truthout.org/articles/pentagon-sued-over-hegseths-new-future-of-warfare-committee-led-by-musk/) · [Tampa Free Press 11/02](https://www.tampafp.com/who-controls-the-war-machine-lawsuit-targets-pentagon-and-elon-musk-led-panel/) |
| 2026-11-03 | Defense Daily (paywalled — headline only): the complaint claims "the incentive grows for the Defense Department to steer contracts to member companies such as SpaceX and Anduril." The photo the Defense Department described as the 'first meeting of all members' was taken 10/1 | ⑥ [Defense Daily 11/03](https://www.defensedaily.com/federal-watchdogs-file-project-meridian-lawsuit/pentagon/) |
| 2026-11-04 (KST) | News watcher detection (Common Dreams · Defense Daily) — **day 2** since filing | `data/spacex_watch.json` due |
| Filings | **No SpaceX 8-K, IR or statement** (latest on EDGAR is the 10/26 8-K Item 8.01 GPU lease). SpaceX is not a defendant, and the legal proceedings note (R25) of the 10-Q (10/22) predates the filing and so does not include this case. Defense Department · MITRE: no response to requests for comment from Military.com and Common Dreams. Musk · Gingrich: no response to October Politico inquiries; Anduril issued a statement: "if an actual conflict of interest arises, we will comply with the highest ethical standards" | ① [EDGAR filing list](https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001181412.json), accessed 2026-11-04 · [10-Q R25](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066880/R25.htm) · ⑥ reports above |

**Discrepancies between sources (recorded)**: ⓐ **Number and order of meetings** — Military.com (citing the complaint) "first SCIF gathering on the day of the 9/30 announcement + second meeting 10/1 (Cotton·Sheehy)" / Defense Daily "the Defense Department described the 10/1 photo as the 'first meeting of all members'" / Politico 10/2 "2 (Cotton·Phil Hegseth attended)" — reads as a difference over whether the 9/30 gathering counts as a 'meeting,' but unconfirmed since the complaint's text was not read ⓑ **Anduril Navy contract** — Common Dreams "$2 billion (CNBC 10/6)" vs OCBJ (citing CNBC) "up to $2.9 billion" — appears to be a difference in how the ceiling is stated, but the CNBC original (404) was not verified, **number not adopted** (unrelated to the SpaceX determination) ⓒ **Number of members** — the MITRE roster gives 3 + 17 = 20, while the complaint says '19 of 21 are private citizens' (reads as including Michael but unconfirmed) ⓓ **Legal status of the co-directors** — the memo has no names; they appear only in the Defense Department press release and speech — how the complaint characterizes the three as 'members' is unconfirmed as the original text was not read ⓔ **Case number · assigned judge** — not given in any report, CourtListener API 401, PACER not accessed (Source: table above · [CourtListener API](https://www.courtlistener.com/api/rest/v4/search/?q=%22Project+Meridian%22&type=r) accessed 2026-11-04, 401).

**Established as fact (3 plaintiff-side announcements + 4 cross-checked reports + government announcement)**: ① Filed 11/2 in D.D.C., 3 plaintiffs, defendants the Defense Department, Hegseth and Michael ② The claims are a declaration of FACA violation, voiding of the memo, barring of activity, and release of records ③ Project Meridian was established by the 9/30 memo with a reporting deadline of 2027-01-28 ④ Musk is a co-director per the Defense Department announcement ⑤ SpaceX is not a party. **Unconfirmed**: the complaint's original text (neither PDF could be rendered by the tools), case number · judge, whether a preliminary injunction was sought, Musk's SGE status, the full roster of all 21 members, the Defense Department's official response (Source: table above).

### 1-1. What this event touches

| Item | Content | Determination |
|---|---|---|
| Axis E · 'Musk risk' | The September issue's Axis E design set only regulation (FAA · overseas licensing), orbital environment, geopolitics (conflict involvement) and federal contracts as milestones, and **has no milestone measuring Musk's government role or conflicts of interest**. This case falls into that blank — even if the court finds a FACA violation, there is no direct path to SpaceX's profit and loss (not a defendant · not a claim to void contracts). There are two paths that could reach it: ⓐ if Musk is an SGE, 18 U.S.C. §208 bars participation in 'particular matters' involving SpaceX's interests — status undisclosed, so no determination possible ⓑ if the advisory committee's recommendations come out as 'prioritize drones and space assets' (statement by a former official in NPR), it would be an **upside** backdrop for E-2027-4 (federal contract awards), but those recommendations require congressional approval and the lawsuit asks the court to block their implementation | Background record · whether to add a milestone is for the monthly issue |
| Axis E · E-2027-4 (new US federal contract awards at or above prior year) | NPR tally 'SpaceX 2026 defense contracts exceed $8 billion' (based on government notices) — not a year-over-year USAspending comparison, so **not a progress input**, recorded as a reference value only. The complaint does not allege the fact of 'steering contracts' | Remains undetermined · reference value recorded |
| Axis E · E-2027-3 (conflict involvement) · T7 | Political exposure overlaps — Senator Shaheen, who issued a statement opposing Meridian, is the same person as in T7 ⓐ (leading the request for an inspector general investigation). But this case is unrelated to the definition of conflict involvement (definitions.conflict_intervention) | Remains unmet (no change) |
| Axis C · AI | NPR: the Defense Department uses Grok — evidence that government AI revenue exists, but the amount is undisclosed (the government customer entry in the 10-Q customer concentration note remains unread) | Background record |
| Probability rules R1–R6 | No lawsuit, government advisory role or conflict of interest in the conditions | Not triggered |
| Financials | No numbers — not subject to litigation reserves (not a defendant) | Not adopted |
| Trigger | Not among existing T1–T10 → **T11 added** (Section 5) | Added |

(Source: `state.milestones[E-2027-3·E-2027-4]` · `state.definitions.conflict_intervention` · [NPR 10/06 (WFAE reprint)](https://www.wfae.org/united-states-world/2026-10-06/elon-musk-and-palmer-luckeys-new-pentagon-roles-raise-ethics-worries) · [Military.com 11/03](https://www.military.com/hegseths-future-of-warfare-panel-is-stacked-with-contractors-who-stand-to-profit-lawsuit-says) · Section 1 table)

**Judgment-layer record**: Project Meridian itself (the 9/30 announcement · the 10/6 NPR conflict-of-interest article · the 10/2 Politico piece) was **absent from both the October and November issues** — it is an event only the news watcher could catch among the four measurement-layer watchers (filings · IR · launches · news), and the news watcher classified it as 'major' only once the lawsuit (11/2) appeared. Musk's change in government role (return after DOGE) is itself an Axis E event, but it had no place in the rules table and so slipped by for a month. Whether the news watcher's queries include a 'CEO government role · conflict of interest' category is registered as a matter for the measurement layer (Source: `reports/2026-10.md` · `reports/2026-11.md` · `data/spacex_watch.json`).
